theory.intro: A **net** of a prism is a flat pattern that folds up to make the solid. A right prism has two identical **end faces** (its cross-section) joined by one **rectangle** for every side of the end face.
facts: A right prism is named after its cross-section: a **triangular** prism has triangular ends and a **hexagonal** prism has hexagonal ends.
A cube and a rectangular prism have rectangular ends.
The net of a right prism with an $n$-sided base is made of **$2$ base polygons** and **$n$ rectangles**, one per edge of the base.
Matching edges must have equal lengths.
The faces must be arranged so they fold into the solid without overlap or gaps; having the correct shapes and number of faces alone is not enough.
When the net folds, each rectangle joins one edge of the base, so that side of the rectangle equals that edge.
steps: For a naming question, find the two identical end polygons and name the prism after their shape.
For a sketching question, draw the end faces and the rectangles that join their edges, using the given lengths.
Check that matching edges have equal lengths and that the arrangement folds without overlap or gaps.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The two identical end faces are rhombi. Four rectangles join their four edges, with matching edge lengths.
The strip folds around the ends to make a rhombic prism.

workedExamples.question_text: Sketch an accurate net for an open rectangular box $6$ cm long, $4$ cm wide and $1.5$ cm high. Label the lengths.
Sketch a net for a right triangular prism with right-angled end triangles whose sides are $3$ cm, $4$ cm and $5$ cm. The prism is $7$ cm long. Label the lengths.

foundation.solution_text:
The net has two identical triangles and three rectangles.
The triangle edges match the rectangle widths, and the strip folds around the triangles without overlap or gaps.
The solid is a triangular prism.

The net is made of six rectangles arranged in a cross.
A solid with two identical rectangular ends joined by rectangles is a rectangular prism.
The solid is a rectangular prism.

The net is made of six identical squares in a cross.
Six equal squares fold up into a cube.
The solid is a cube.

The net has two identical six-sided end faces and six rectangles, one for each side of the hexagon.
Two identical hexagons joined by rectangles fold up into a hexagonal prism.
The solid is a hexagonal prism.

development.solution_text:
The two identical end faces each have four sides with one pair parallel — they are trapeziums.
There are four rectangles, one for each side of the trapezium.
Their widths match the trapezium's edges in order, and the arrangement folds without overlap or gaps.
The solid is a trapezoidal prism.

development.question_text: Sketch an accurate net for an open rectangular box $8$ cm long, $5$ cm wide and $2$ cm high. Label the lengths.
development.solution_text:
Draw an $8\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}$ base.
Attach an $8\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$ rectangle to each $8$ cm edge and a $5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$ rectangle to each $5$ cm edge.
These four sides fold upwards around the base with matching edges and no overlap or gaps. Leave the top open.

development.question_text: Sketch a net for a right triangular prism with a right-angled end triangle whose sides are $6$ cm, $8$ cm and $10$ cm. The prism is $12$ cm long. Label the lengths.
development.solution_text:
Draw a strip of rectangles $6\text{ cm}\times12\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}\times12\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}\times12\text{ cm}$, joined along their $12$ cm edges in that order.
Attach one $6$–$8$–$10$ right-angled triangle to each of the two opposite $8$ cm edges of the middle rectangle.
The rectangle widths match the triangle edges. The strip folds around the triangles without overlap or gaps.

mastery.question_text: Sketch an accurate net for an open rectangular box $12.5$ cm long, $7.5$ cm wide and $3.5$ cm high. Label the lengths.
mastery.solution_text:
Draw a $12.5\text{ cm}\times7.5\text{ cm}$ base.
Attach a $12.5\text{ cm}\times3.5\text{ cm}$ rectangle to each $12.5$ cm edge and a $7.5\text{ cm}\times3.5\text{ cm}$ rectangle to each $7.5$ cm edge.
The four sides fold upwards with matching edges and no overlap or gaps. Leave the top open.

mastery.question_text: Sketch a net for a right triangular prism with a right-angled end triangle whose sides are $7.5$ cm, $10$ cm and $12.5$ cm. The prism is $14.5$ cm long. Label the lengths.
mastery.solution_text:
Draw a strip of rectangles $7.5\text{ cm}\times14.5\text{ cm}$, $10\text{ cm}\times14.5\text{ cm}$ and $12.5\text{ cm}\times14.5\text{ cm}$, joined along their $14.5$ cm edges in that order.
Attach one right-angled triangle with sides $7.5$ cm, $10$ cm and $12.5$ cm to each of the two opposite $10$ cm edges of the middle rectangle.
The rectangle widths match the triangle edges, and the arrangement folds without overlap or gaps.
